title: Grade 12 Physics — Wave Optics
description: Huygens' principle, interference, diffraction, and polarisation
subject: physics

questions.question: Huygens' Principle states that every point on a wavefront:
options: Acts as a secondary source of spherical wavelets; the common tangent to these wavelets gives the new wavefront
questions.explanation: Huygens' Principle: each point on a wavefront is a secondary source of spherical wavelets. The envelope (tangent) of these secondary wavelets after time t gives the new wavefront. Used to explain reflection, refraction, diffraction.

questions.question: In Young's Double Slit Experiment, bright fringes form when the path difference is:
questions.explanation: Constructive interference (bright fringe): path difference = nλ (integer multiple of wavelength). Destructive (dark fringe): path difference = (2n−1)λ/2 (odd multiple of λ/2). n = 0: central bright fringe.

questions.question: Fringe width β in YDSE (slit separation d, screen distance D, wavelength λ) is:
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d. Increasing D or λ increases fringe width; increasing d decreases it. Central fringe is bright. All fringes are equally spaced (equal β).

questions.question: Coherent sources are sources that:
options: Have the same frequency and a constant phase difference
questions.explanation: Coherent sources: same frequency (or wavelength) and constant (not necessarily zero) phase difference. Required for sustained interference. In YDSE, both slits are illuminated by one source → coherent.

questions.question: In diffraction at a single slit, the central maximum is _____ the secondary maxima.
questions.explanation: Single-slit diffraction: central maximum width = 2λD/a (a = slit width). Secondary maxima: each has width λD/a. Central maximum = twice the width of secondary maxima. Also: central max is much more intense.

questions.question: Polarisation of light proves that light is a:
questions.explanation: Polarisation is possible only for transverse waves (not longitudinal). Light can be polarised by polaroids, reflection (Brewster's angle), refraction, scattering. This proves light is a transverse EM wave.

questions.question: Malus' Law states that the intensity of plane polarised light after passing through an analyser is:
questions.explanation: Malus' Law: I = I₀ cos²θ where θ = angle between transmission axis of analyser and plane of polarisation. At θ=0°: I = I₀ (maximum). At θ=90°: I = 0 (complete extinction).

questions.question: Brewster's angle (iB) is the angle of incidence at which reflected light is:
options: Completely plane polarised (perpendicular to plane of incidence)
questions.explanation: Brewster's angle: reflected light is 100% polarised (s-polarised). Brewster's Law: tan iB = n (refractive index). At iB, reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular.

questions.question: Resolving power of an optical instrument depends on:
options: The wavelength of light used — shorter λ = better resolution
questions.explanation: Resolving power = ability to distinguish two closely spaced objects. Rayleigh criterion: θ_min = 1.22λ/D. Shorter wavelength (blue light, X-rays) = better resolution. Electron microscopes use very short λ (de Broglie wavelength).

questions.question: In YDSE, when the screen is moved farther from the slits (D increases), the fringe width:
questions.explanation: β = λD/d. Increasing D directly increases β. This is why YDSE is done at a large screen distance — to make fringes wide enough to observe.

questions.question: If the YDSE experiment is conducted in water (refractive index n), fringe width compared to air:
options: Decreases by factor n (wavelength in water = λ/n)
questions.explanation: In medium with refractive index n: λ_medium = λ_air/n. Since β = λD/d: β_water = (λ/n)D/d = β_air/n. Fringe width decreases in denser medium.

questions.question: Diffraction is the bending of light around:
options: Obstacles or through narrow openings (comparable to wavelength of light)
questions.explanation: Diffraction: bending of light (or any wave) around obstacles or through small apertures, especially when the size of the obstacle/aperture ≈ wavelength. Explains why light bends around corners slightly.

questions.question: The condition for dark fringes (minima) in single-slit diffraction is: a sinθ = ?
questions.explanation: Single-slit minima: a sinθ = nλ (n = ±1, ±2,...). Central maximum is at θ = 0. Secondary minima are at sinθ = ±λ/a, ±2λ/a, etc.

questions.question: Scattering of light by small particles explains why the sky is blue and sunsets are red. This is called:
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering: I ∝ 1/λ⁴. Blue light (λ~450nm) scatters ~5× more than red (λ~700nm). Sky appears blue. At sunset: long path through atmosphere; blue scattered away; red/orange reaches eyes.

questions.question: LASER (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation) produces:
options: Coherent, monochromatic, highly directional, and intense light
questions.explanation: LASER properties: (1) Coherent — fixed phase relationship; (2) Monochromatic — single wavelength; (3) Highly collimated/directional; (4) Very intense. Applications: surgery, data storage, communications, cutting.
